changed_since_round_1.change: Doubled the Youth Studio block from 2 to 4 additional sessions a month (6 to 12 sessions for the quarter) at the same £6,500.
changed_since_round_1.why: updates/U3 is a written clarification from the partner: its own funding cut halved delivery in June 2024, it holds a 40-name waiting list, and it can supply staff for up to four extra sessions a month at the same £6,500. Round 1 bought only half of what the same money now buys. The £6,500 line and the total are unchanged.

changed_since_round_1.change: Raised the Youth Studio targets from 780 to 1,000 visits and from 120 to 140 monthly unique participants.
changed_since_round_1.why: 18 sessions instead of 12. 1,000 visits is 55.6 per session, a 25% discount to the current 74 per session, because the block is not linear: the first six extra sessions draw on the waitlist, the second six have to fill from the same base. 140 is 115 current participants plus 25 of the 40-name waitlist.

changed_since_round_1.change: Added a hard 60-attendee cap to every evening event, with pre-booking, a door count, a hard stop at 60, a turnaway log, and a new metric (M13).
changed_since_round_1.why: updates/U2 adds a building-control condition: the accessible entrance must be operable before any evening event with more than 60 attendees is licensed, whether or not it uses the first floor. The entrance is not operable and the repair is capital, so the cap is a licence condition, not a target. The 180-seat hall is no longer the binding capacity.

changed_since_round_1.change: Changed the mailer from one dated evening to two dated evenings with a booking route, reserved half of each mailed date's places for Northside and Kiln Field bookings until 48 hours before, and removed the mailer from the G0 fallback package.
changed_since_round_1.why: Under a 60-attendee cap, a single dated offer risks turning away the estate residents the pilot exists to reach. Two dates spread demand; the reservation protects the priority audience from the cap. The mailer cost is unchanged at £4,200. Because it is now built around two dated pilot evenings, it is not committed if the pilot is not; the fallback is Studio + training (£9,300).

changed_since_round_1.change: Retained the 640 evening-visit target but added a cap-constrained reading rule: attendance plus recorded turnaways counts as the demand floor.
changed_since_round_1.why: 640 is 49.2 per opening across 13 openings (82% of the cap) or 53.3 across 12 programmed sessions (89% of the cap); the 2023 effect of +38% would be 54.9 per session, or 91.4% of the cap. The cap can censor a successful result, so turnaways must be counted and reported alongside attendance rather than treated as an anecdote.

changed_since_round_1.change: Updated the lift everywhere to £27,500 and an 8-week lead, and revised the capital recommendation: the cheapest coherent package containing the lift is now £51,500, £3,500 over the envelope.
changed_since_round_1.why: updates/U2 re-quoted the work and added the 60-attendee condition. Round 1 could describe a lift + evening + bus package at £46,000 that fitted by deleting the Studio; the re-quote removes that option. Lift + evening + bus + Studio is £58,000, £10,000 over. The lift must be a separate capital bid, instructed as early as possible so the 8-week lead does not consume a programme quarter.

changed_since_round_1.change: Revised the assessment's awareness finding from 'awareness is not the binding constraint' to 'awareness is uneven, not absent'.
changed_since_round_1.why: updates/U1 finds that 48% of households across Northside and Kiln Field have never heard of the centre, 37% have heard but never attended, and only 15% have attended at least once. Round 1's claim was based on the 2022 borough print null, which did not measure estate awareness. The 2022 null still stands for borough-wide print; it does not support the stronger claim that awareness is irrelevant.

changed_since_round_1.change: Upgraded the targeted mailer from the weakest line in the budget to the evidenced response to a measured awareness gap, while keeping its week-4 stop rule.
changed_since_round_1.why: updates/U1 gives the mailer a specific audience and a measured gap. It remains a test, not a certainty: the equalities team says it has not tested whether awareness alone converts, and the 2022 package already included a mail-drop that produced no detectable effect. Hence one wave, two dates, and S5 (fewer than 30 registrations means no repeat).

changed_since_round_1.change: Recorded cost as an unaddressed barrier: 22% of aware estate households name cost as the main barrier, and the quoted menu contains no ticket or fare subsidy.
changed_since_round_1.why: updates/U1's barrier split is 57% transport, 22% cost, 11% programme content. The plan can act on transport and awareness, but it cannot invent a subsidy. Recording it prevents the report from claiming that access has been improved across the board.

changed_since_round_1.change: Removed the café equipment refresh from the option set as no longer available, rather than as rejected on merit.
changed_since_round_1.why: updates/U4 defers the refresh to the next financial year and says it is no longer available this quarter. The supplier change has no programming or budget effect and prices to visitors are unchanged. The café was already unfunded, so the revenue plan and total are unchanged.

changed_since_round_1.change: Renamed uncertainty IDs to UNC- to avoid collision with the update file IDs, resolved the old partner-capacity uncertainty, and added new uncertainties for the 60-cap scope and the cost barrier.
changed_since_round_1.why: Updates are numbered U1-U4; the round-1 uncertainties were also U1-U14, which made references ambiguous. UNC-4 is now largely resolved by updates/U3; UNC-3 covers whether the 60 condition catches the Youth Studio; UNC-10 covers cost; UNC-7 now includes cap censoring.

changed_since_round_1.change: Revised cost-effectiveness: Youth Studio about £14 per additional visit (was £25); blended about £59 (was £90); evening unchanged at about £147.
changed_since_round_1.why: The same £6,500 now buys 12 sessions and a target of 476 additional visits rather than 6 sessions and 256. The Studio target is not doubled because the marginal sessions are harder to fill. The evening ratio is unchanged because both its cost and its target are unchanged.

changed_since_round_1.change: Revised stop rule S6, added S7 (cap saturation) and added a cap-breach incident rule (C1).
changed_since_round_1.why: The partner has already confirmed the block in writing, so the old S6 (partner cannot confirm 3 sessions a month) is obsolete; the new failure mode is a delivery shortfall against a block price. The 60 cap creates two new failure modes: saturation, which should trigger the capital case, and breach, which is a licensing incident rather than a missed target.

changed_since_round_1.change: Kept the revenue allocation and the £37,500 total unchanged; the £10,500 headroom still lapses.
changed_since_round_1.why: Every changed item either costs the same (Studio, mailer) or is outside the revenue envelope (lift). No new quoted item became available and the café left the menu. A second mailer wave (£4,200, taking the total to £41,700) was considered and not committed because it would have to be bought before the week-4 result exists. The plan still fits a 15% reduced envelope of £40,800 with £3,300 to spare.

allocations.item: Evening opening, 13 weeks (responsible person + utilities + cleaning)
Late bus subsidy: one minibus on the Northside-Kiln Field loop, 13 weeks
Additional Youth Studio sessions: up to 4 per month for the quarter (12 sessions, same £6,500 block price)
Staff training: welcome and access awareness, 2 days
Targeted mailer to priority-neighbourhood households (two dated evenings, booking route)

chosen_pilot.name: Evening Access Pilot
chosen_pilot.why: It remains the only intervention in the pack that has already been tested at this venue, and it was tested in the most informative way available: the 2023 evening programme drew 38% more attendance year-on-year with a minibus, then fell back to pre-pilot level within six weeks of the minibus stopping, with the new estate attendees gone. Same building, same programme, same staff, weeks apart - that isolates transport rather than programme or awareness as the binding constraint. updates/U1 sharpens the case: among estate households that have heard of the centre, 57% name getting home after an evening event as the main barrier, while 48% have never heard of it at all, which is why the pilot pairs transport with a targeted, dated offer. It is also the only instrument that reaches Northside and Kiln Field by construction, because the minibus goes to them and nowhere else, and the only proposal whose failure would teach the board something before it commits to a recurrent transport line. Opening and transport are funded as one unit because funding either alone reproduces a known failure: opening without the bus is the six weeks of 2023 that did not work, and the bus without opening delivers people to a closed door. The pilot now runs under a hard 60-attendee cap until the accessible entrance is operable (updates/U2); it complies by pre-booking, counting at the door, stopping entry at 60 and logging turnaways, and it treats those turnaways as evidence for the separate capital bid rather than as a reason to breach the licence.
target_segments: Estate households that have never heard of the centre (48% of the two estates)
Lapsed Evening Talks attendees from the pre-July-2024 cohort
Public-transport-dependent working adults excluded by the 19:10 last bus

evidence_assessment.claim: 92% of visitors are satisfied or very satisfied (285/310), described as a robust picture of how our audiences feel.
evidence_assessment.limitation: Self-selected forms handed out at Family Saturdays on one free-entry weekend. No sampling frame, no non-response data, no weighting. 78% of respondents attended with children under 12 and 71% travelled by car, so the pool is structurally a car-driving family audience. It says nothing about non-attenders, weekday audiences or evening audiences, and cannot support 'our audiences'.

evidence_assessment.claim: It covers the people who come on a Saturday; we did not survey people who do not come, and weekday and evening audiences were not in the room.
evidence_assessment.limitation: The author disclaims the generalisation the headline invites. This is the most important line in the survey file and it should govern how the 92% is quoted to the board and the council.

evidence_assessment.claim: Visits fell from 610 in Q1 2024 (12 sessions) to 444 in Q1 2025 (6 sessions).
evidence_assessment.limitation: Does not show falling demand. Sessions were halved from 4 to 2 per month from June 2024, which accounts for the visit decline on its own. updates/U3 confirms this was a funding cut at the partner, not a change in interest.

evidence_assessment.claim: Visits per session rose from 50.8 (Jan-May 2024) to 67.8 (Jun 2024-Mar 2025), and monthly unique participants rose from 71 in Jan 2024 to 115 in Mar 2025, up 62% on half the sessions.
evidence_assessment.limitation: Strong evidence that the Studio is capacity-constrained, now confirmed by the partner's written clarification (updates/U3) and its 40-name waiting list. It still does not establish the room's capacity or the fill rate of a tripled session block.

evidence_assessment.source: interviews.md - youth worker, updated by updates/U3
evidence_assessment.claim: The youth worker speculated that numbers were down because young people had moved on; the same answer said sessions run less often because of staffing and fill when they run.
evidence_assessment.limitation: The speculative first half has been withdrawn in writing by the partner organisation. The second half is corroborated by the attendance series and by the partner's own account of its funding cut. It is no longer evidence of a demand problem and should not be quoted as one.

evidence_assessment.claim: Most regulars drive; the two estates are a bus change and a walk away; the last bus back is 19:10, so anything finishing after seven is no use to them.
evidence_assessment.limitation: One practitioner's account, not a measurement. It is raised in confidence because it triangulates with the survey's 71% car-travel figure, the hard 19:10 last service in constraints.md, and the 57% transport barrier in updates/U1.

evidence_assessment.claim: The last service back leaves the centre stop at 19:10 on weekdays, and there is no staffed car park after 20:00.
evidence_assessment.limitation: A hard operating fact that converts the transport claim from opinion into a constraint, but it does not quantify how many people are excluded or where they live.

evidence_assessment.claim: Evening attendance was 38% higher year-on-year with a paid late minibus and most new attendees came from the two priority estates; after the minibus funding ran out the programme continued six weeks without it, attendance fell back to roughly pre-pilot level and the new estate attendees stopped coming.
evidence_assessment.limitation: Not a controlled trial: no comparison group, single quarter, single site, and the ending is confounded with the abruptness of the funding stop and with season. The reversal within weeks in the same site and programme is nonetheless the strongest identification in the pack. It says nothing about whether the effect would survive a second quarter, and the 2023 comparison was uncapped while this quarter is capped at 60.

evidence_assessment.source: prior-interventions.md - 2022 borough print and poster campaign
evidence_assessment.claim: £9,000 on posters and leaflets plus a mail-drop produced attendance within normal seasonal variation, word of mouth still dominant at 64%, and no measurable change in first-time attendance from the priority estates; the board minuted: do not repeat the poster spend without a specific audience and a specific offer.
evidence_assessment.limitation: Establishes that generic borough-wide print produced no detectable effect here; it does not prove print can never work. The 2022 package included a mail-drop, a direct caution against assuming a mailer alone will move attendance. It did not measure estate awareness, so updates/U1's 48% 'never heard' does not contradict it but does limit how far it can be generalised.

evidence_assessment.claim: Evening Talks stopped last summer and nobody told her, so she assumed the whole thing had ended; the problem is communication, not the programme.
evidence_assessment.limitation: n=1, and the attendance series partly contradicts the severity: Evening Talks returned in Sep 2024 at 61 unique participants, higher than any month before the gap, and rose to 66 by Nov 2024. Most of the audience returned without being told.

evidence_assessment.source: constraints.md - venue, licence and staffing, updated by updates/U2
evidence_assessment.claim: Main hall holds 180 seated; the accessible entrance and passenger lift are out of service so no first-floor public event is permitted; the lift is capital, now £27,500 with an 8-week lead, cannot be phased; and the accessible entrance must be operable before any evening event with more than 60 attendees is licensed, whether or not it uses the first floor. 1.5 FTE front-of-house and no events manager post, with evening opening requiring a named responsible person the rota does not staff.
evidence_assessment.limitation: States the barriers with certainty but gives no measure of how many visitors they exclude, because the centre holds no disability or access data. The 60-attendee condition is a hard capacity constraint on the evening programme and may or may not catch non-licensed Youth Studio sessions (UNC-3). The staffing position sits in tension with the £9,600 evening line, which assumes existing staff are extended rather than a new post created.

evidence_assessment.source: resources.md - envelope and quoted costs, updated by updates/U3 and updates/U4
evidence_assessment.claim: £48,000 for the quarter committed at the start with no carry-over; a closed menu of quoted items; capital and revenue cannot be swapped without a council variation; anything not on the list needs a written quote and so cannot be in this quarter's plan. The partner can supply up to 4 extra Youth Studio sessions a month at the same £6,500. The café equipment refresh is no longer available this quarter.
evidence_assessment.limitation: The 15% reduction for the following quarter is described as a verbal indication with nothing confirmed and no figure agreed, so it can be stress-tested but not planned against as a number. The closed menu forecloses new posts, commissioned evaluation, ticket subsidies and any transport beyond the single quoted loop. The café is now off the menu, so it cannot even be reconsidered on merit.

evidence_assessment.claim: Monthly sessions, visits and unique participants for five programmes from Jan 2024 to Mar 2025.
evidence_assessment.limitation: Contains no postcode, neighbourhood, age or disability field, so it cannot answer which programmes reach the priority estates - the council's own reporting requirement. unique_participants is a monthly figure and is not deduplicated across months, so quarterly unique totals cannot be produced by summing.

evidence_assessment.source: updates/U1 - council equalities team doorstep survey
evidence_assessment.claim: Of 120 households across Northside and Kiln Field, 48% have never heard of the centre, 37% have heard but never attended, and 15% have attended at least once. Among those who have heard, 57% name getting home after an evening event as the main barrier, 22% name cost, and 11% name programme content. The covering note says awareness has not been tested as a route to attendance.
evidence_assessment.limitation: A doorstep survey of 120 households across two estates, not a probability sample of the borough. The barrier shares rest on roughly 62 households that had heard of the centre, so they carry wide margins and are directional. It measures stated barriers, not behaviour, and cannot say which programmes estate residents use. It is strong enough to retire the claim that awareness is irrelevant, not strong enough to prove that awareness converts.

evidence_assessment.source: updates/U2 - lift contractor re-quote and building control condition
evidence_assessment.claim: Lift repair and accessible entrance reinstatement now £27,500 (was £22,000) with an 8-week lead (was 6); parts must be remanufactured. The accessible entrance must be operable before any evening event with more than 60 attendees is licensed, whether or not it uses the first floor. No other quoted cost changed and the quarter remains 13 weeks.
evidence_assessment.limitation: A supplier price and a regulatory condition, not estimates. Neither says how many disabled visitors are currently excluded. The 60-attendee condition's scope beyond licensed evening events is not defined in the pack (UNC-3).

evidence_assessment.source: updates/U3 - partner youth organisation, in writing
evidence_assessment.claim: The partner's own funding changed in June 2024 and it cut delivery from 4 to 2 sessions a month, which is the whole reason visits fell. Unique participants rose from 71 to 115 and it holds a waiting list of 40. It can supply staff for up to 4 extra sessions a month for the quarter at the same £6,500, using the waitlist first. The youth worker's 'moved on' speculation is withdrawn.
evidence_assessment.limitation: A provider's account of its own funding and capacity, corroborated by the attendance series. It does not guarantee that 12 extra sessions will fill, that the room is on the ground floor, or that the room can absorb a tripled cadence; those are delivery risks (UNC-4, UNC-15).

evidence_assessment.claim: Coffee supplier changes from Bean and Co to Harbour Roasters; the café equipment refresh is deferred to the next financial year and no longer available this quarter; prices to visitors are unchanged; the notice does not change the programming budget.
evidence_assessment.limitation: Says nothing about programming, attendance or the envelope. It removes one option from the menu and creates no new one. It is recorded so that its absence from the plan is not mistaken for an oversight.

metrics.name: Evening attendance (visits)
metrics.target: At least 640 visits across the quarter (+34%; the 2023 pilot delivered +38% year-on-year), or attendance plus recorded turnaways at least 640

metrics.name: Priority-neighbourhood share of evening attendance
metrics.baseline: Not measured - no postcode field exists; first reading week 6
metrics.target: At least 35% of evening attenders resident in Northside or Kiln Field by week 13

metrics.name: Minibus utilisation (passengers per return trip)
metrics.target: Mean of at least 8 by week 6, with a floor of 6 triggering renegotiation

metrics.name: Youth Studio visits
metrics.target: At least 1,000 visits across 18 sessions (55.6 per session, a 25% discount to current performance)

metrics.name: Postcode capture rate
metrics.target: At least 80% of recorded visits from week 6

metrics.name: Family Saturdays visits (guardrail)
metrics.target: At least 1626 - no decline worse than 10%

metrics.name: Community Choir visits (guardrail)
metrics.target: At least 674 - no decline worse than 10%

metrics.name: Evening event finish-time compliance
metrics.baseline: Not applicable - no evening opening currently runs

metrics.name: Named responsible person on duty
metrics.baseline: 0% - the rota does not staff evenings

metrics.name: 60-attendee cap compliance
metrics.target: 0 events counted above 60; 100% of evenings counted at the door; every turnaway logged

metrics.name: Cost per additional visit
metrics.baseline: Not computable - the pack holds no programme cost data
metrics.target: At most £59 blended; at most £14 for the Youth Studio; evening reported separately at about £147

metrics.name: Targeted mailer response
metrics.target: At least 30 attributable registrations by end of week 4, else no repeat

uncertainties: UNC-1: Whether 1.5 FTE front-of-house can roster a named responsible person for 13 Thursday evenings at all - constraints.md says the rota does not staff evenings, while the £9,600 line assumes existing staff are extended. Confirmed or the evening strand is not committed.

UNC-2: Whether the 2023 +38% result reproduces in a different quarter without novelty, and whether the effect outlives the quarter - a single uncontrolled observation is the entire basis for the largest budget line. The 60 cap also makes this quarter's comparison non-identical to 2023.

UNC-3: Whether the new 60-attendee licensing condition catches the Youth Studio and other non-Talks sessions, which currently draw about 74 visits per session. If it does, the Studio's hard ceiling is 1,080 visits and the existing programme may already be over the cap. Confirmed with building control in week 0.

UNC-4: Whether the partner can deliver the confirmed block of 4 extra sessions a month, whether the room is on the ground floor, and whether it can absorb 6 sessions a month. The staffing question is resolved in writing by updates/U3; the delivery and room questions are not.
UNC-5: Whether the operator's 19:15 and 21:30 departures run from the centre or from the estates - it determines the start time and therefore which films can be shown without stranding the audience.

UNC-6: How many people from Northside and Kiln Field currently attend at programme level - updates/U1 gives a household-level 15% ever-attended share but there is still no postcode or equalities data at the door, so the council's reporting requirement cannot yet be met at programme level.

UNC-7: The size of latent evening demand from the estates - the 2023 record says 'the majority of new attendees' without counts, no minibus passenger figures survived, and the 60 cap now censors any demand above 60. Turnaways give a floor, not an estimate.

UNC-8: The human cost of deferring the £27,500 lift repair is real and unmeasured; disabled visitors are excluded now, every evening is capped at 60, and the centre cannot count how many are affected. Deferral is a programme-budget judgement, not a finding that the work is unnecessary. The cheapest coherent package containing the lift is £51,500, £3,500 over.

UNC-9: Whether the council will supply the priority-neighbourhood postcode list that defines Northside and Kiln Field - it is not in this pack, and without it captured postcodes cannot be mapped to estates.

UNC-10: Whether cost is a barrier that could be removed - 22% of aware estate households name it, but the quoted menu has no ticket or fare subsidy and the plan cannot invent one. It is recorded as unaddressed, not solved.
UNC-11: Whether £147 per additional evening visit is good value - the pack holds no programme cost data, so neither that figure nor the £14 Studio figure can be benchmarked against business as usual.
UNC-12: Whether the indicated council reduction happens, and at what size - described as verbal, unconfirmed and with no figure agreed, so it is treated as a stress scenario rather than a budget.

UNC-13: Whether the targeted mailer converts awareness into attendance - updates/U1 shows a real 48% awareness gap, but the equalities team has not tested conversion and the failed 2022 package already included a mail-drop. The week-4 response count is the test.
UNC-14: Whether thirteen extra evenings displace or degrade the weekday and Saturday programme by stretching the same 1.5 FTE team, and whether the 10% guardrail would catch it early enough.

UNC-15: The Youth Studio room's capacity at 6 sessions a month - constraints.md gives the main hall at 180 seats but says nothing about the Studio, so the 1,000-visit target assumes the space can absorb a tripled cadence and the waitlist converts.
UNC-16: Whether unaccompanied young people travelling home at 21:30 fall within the partner's existing safeguarding policy, and who is responsible if they do not.
